name: Lola Jeong
life: “I still remember the lucky charm sewn into our practice curtain.” Thursday often includes a stop at Tideline Market, where Lola picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I came to return a button my wife thought unlucky. It won somebody else the costume prize.
appearance: Lola is easy to recognize by a blunt cut just below the ears and two dimples that appear only with a full smile. Usually dressed in a plum-colored cardigan with a little coil of soft measuring tape, Lola gives a little nod before asking a hard question when listening.
personality: Lola treats a small promise with the gravity others reserve for a contract. This makes Lola lovely to rely on and surprisingly difficult to invite on a whim.
agenda: To explain the returned lucky button to its next wearer.
family: Percy Andrade is Lola’s older cousin. Lola can always ask for five minutes alone. Percy asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Low water music*, Percy says, “I scraped my knee there and have called it a much ruder name since.”
connections: Milo Rizzo. The yellow winter-coat button acquires a new history in the costume box. Also in the story is Nelson Gallagher (button donor).

reactions.situation: The donor recognizes the uniform it came from
reactions.response: Lola asks the owner which garment the donor wants remembered.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Lola lets the child choose whether to stand by the door or sit beside the window while another adult gets help.

reactions.situation: When offered a favor with ambiguous terms
reactions.response: Lola says what can be returned and asks whether that will do.
